source_text: III. Ζωγρηθέντων δὲ αὐτῶν καὶ λαβόντων ἄρτον ἅγιον καὶ ὕδωρ τῷ σαββάτῳ ἐπέστη αὐτοῖς Πολέμων ὁ νεωκόρος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ τεταγμένοι ἀναζητεῖν καὶ ἕλκειν τοὺς Χριστιανοὺς ἐπιθύειν καὶ μιαροφαγεῖν. Καί φησιν ὁ νεωκόρος· Οἴδατε πάντως διάταγμα τοῦ αὐτοκράτορος, ὡς κελεύει ὑμᾶς ἐπιθύειν τοῖς θεοῖς. Καὶ ὁ Πιόνιος ἔφη· Οἴδαμεν τὰ προστάγματα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν οἷς κελεύει ἡμᾶς αὐτῷ μόνῳ προσκυνεῖν. Πολέμων εἶπεν· Ἔλθετε οὖν εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν κἀκεῖ πεισθήσεσθε. Καὶ ἡ Σαβῖνα καὶ ὁ Ἀσκληπιάδης ἔφησαν· Ἡμεῖς θεῷ ζῶντι πειθόμεθα. Ἦγεν οὖν αὐτοὺς οὐ μετὰ βίας. Καὶ προελθόντων αὐτῶν εἶδον πάντες ὅτι δεσμὰ ἐφόρουν, καὶ ὡς ἐπὶ παραδόξῳ συνέδραμεν ἐν τάχει ὄχλος ὥστε ὠθεῖν ἀλλήλους. Καὶ ἐλθόντων εἰς τὴν ἀγοράν, ἐν τῇ στοᾷ τῇ ἀνατολικῇ, ἐν τῇ διπυλίδι, ἐγεμίσθη πᾶσα ἡ ἀγορὰ καὶ αἱ ὑπερῷαι στοαὶ Ἑλλήνων τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων καὶ γυναικῶν· ἐσχόλαζον γὰρ διὰ τὸ εἶναι μέγα σάββατον. Ἀνίεσαν δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ βάθρα καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ κιβώτια σκοποῦντες.
pass_a_gloss: But after they had been caught alive and had received holy bread and water on the sabbath, Polemon the temple-warden and those ordered with him to search for and drag Christians to sacrifice and to eat defiled food came upon them. And the warden says: You certainly know the emperor's edict, that it commands you to sacrifice to the gods. And Pionius said: We know the orders of God in which he commands us to bow down to him alone. Polemon said: Come then to the marketplace and there you will be persuaded. And Sabina and Asclepiades said: We obey the living God. He led them therefore without violence. And as they advanced everyone saw that they were wearing chains, and as if at a strange sight a crowd ran together quickly so that they pushed one another. And when they arrived at the marketplace, at the eastern stoa, at the double-gate, the whole marketplace and the upper stoas were filled with Greeks and Jews and women; for they were free from work because it was a great sabbath. And they were even climbing up onto the steps and onto the chests to observe.
pass_b_english: After they had been arrested and had taken the holy bread and water on the Sabbath, Polemon the temple-warden came upon them with the men assigned with him to hunt out Christians and drag them to sacrifice and to eat food defiled by idols. The warden said, You surely know the emperor's decree, which commands you to sacrifice to the gods. Pionius answered, We know the commandments of God, in which he commands us to worship him alone. Polemon said, Come then to the marketplace, and there you will be made to comply. Sabina and Asclepiades answered, We obey the living God. So he brought them without using force.

As they walked on, all the onlookers saw that they wore chains, and as though at some marvel a crowd rushed together at speed, so that they jostled one another. When they reached the marketplace, at the eastern colonnade by the double gate, the whole marketplace and the galleries above were crowded with Greeks and Jews and women, for they were at leisure because it was a great Sabbath. People even clambered up onto the stands and onto the boxes to get a view.
